content.text:
Found the bug. The header has both classes `file-list-header bin-list-header`. The base `.file-list-header` sets a 3-column grid (`1fr 120px 180px`) and `.bin-list-header` sets a 5-column grid (`1fr 180px 100px 80px 90px`). Since both have the same CSS specificity, the one loaded later in the cascade wins — and with Vite's CSS handling, `.file-list-header` from the globally-imported `App.css` can override the component-imported `bin-browser.css`.

The `bin-list-header` already has all the styling it needs (font, padding, border, etc.) — it's a complete duplicate of the base styles. The fix is to remove the `file-list-header` class from the bin header element.

Let me also check if the items have the same issue.

Good — `BinListItem` only uses `bin-list-item` (no `file-list-item` class), so the row items are fine. The problem is only with the header.

The fix is simple — remove `file-list-header` from the bin header's className since `bin-list-header` already defines all the same base styles:

content.text:
The fix: removed the `file-list-header` class from the bin header element at `BinBrowser.tsx:362`.

The root cause was a CSS specificity conflict. Both `.file-list-header` (from `file-browser.css`, imported globally via `App.css`) and `.bin-list-header` (from `bin-browser.css`, imported by the component) define `grid-template-columns` with the same specificity (one class selector). The base class defines a 3-column grid (`1fr 120px 180px`) while the bin class defines the correct 5-column grid (`1fr 180px 100px 80px 90px`). Depending on Vite's CSS load order, the 3-column grid was winning, causing the 5 header items to wrap across two rows.

Since `bin-list-header` already contains all the styling it needs (display, padding, font, border, etc.), the `file-list-header` class was unnecessary and only caused conflicts.
